Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediCore Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO; Maria Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MediCore Devices had a productive Q3, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance: organic revenue growth by segment and geography; SG&A expense management and efficiency gains; procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary; competitive dynamics and market share trends; strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter; and key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Maria will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

I'm pleased to report that total organic revenue growth came in at 9.2% year-over-year, excluding the impact of our recent acquisition of NeuroStim Solutions and foreign exchange fluctuations. This acceleration from 7.8% in Q2 marks our strongest quarterly performance since pre-pandemic levels, driven by robust procedural volume recovery in elective procedures, favorable product mix shifts toward high-margin consumables, and early traction from our innovation pipeline.

Starting with our segments across our four key franchises: Cardiovascular & Structural Interventions, or CVI, at 42% of total revenue; Orthopaedics & Spine; Advanced Surgical Technologies, or AST; and Diabetes & Patient Monitoring, or DPM.

CVI delivered 12.4% organic growth, fueled by double-digit gains across transcatheter aortic valve replacement, or TAVR, peripheral vascular interventions, and cardiac rhythm management. TAVR procedural volumes grew 15% globally, benefiting from expanded indications for our next-gen EvoFlow valve, which now captures 28% U.S. market share, up from 24% a year ago, closing the gap on leaders like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform. We also saw 11% growth in ablation catheters for atrial fibrillation, driven by our AI-enhanced RhythmSync mapping system, which reduced procedure times by 22% in clinical trials and is driving surgeon adoption. Average selling prices held steady at plus 1%, offsetting some reimbursement headwinds under CMS's prior authorization rules.

Orthopaedics & Spine grew 7.1% organically, with hips and knees up 9%, outpacing the U.S. market's 5-6% procedural growth per AAOS data. Our cementless Triad hip system, launched last year, contributed 2 points of growth through mix shift, as it commands a 15% premium ASP over legacy systems. Spine was softer at plus 4%, impacted by hospital capital budget constraints, but our Mobi-C cervical disc—now with Level 1 evidence from our PROSPECT study—drove 18% growth in motion preservation. We're gaining share from DePuy Synthes in enabling technologies like our 3D-printed VerteFix implants.

AST posted 8.9% organic growth, led by our Hugo robotic-assisted surgery platform, which saw 25% procedure growth in soft tissue applications, narrowing the gap with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci dominance. Consumables recurring revenue—our endoscopy single-use scopes and staplers—jumped 14%, reflecting a shift from reprocessing amid infection control scrutiny post-COVID. U.S. hospital outsourcing trends boosted our VCare vision systems by 20%.

DPM rounded out at 6.3% growth, with continuous glucose monitoring sensors up 10% on strong refill demand for our Liberty Patch system, competing effectively with Dexcom G7 and Abbott Freestyle Libre. Patient monitoring capital sales softened to plus 2% due to lingering inventory destocking, but connected care software subscriptions grew 22%, aligning with value-based care mandates like CMS's Bundled Payments for Care Improvement.

Procedural volumes across segments rose 11% globally, with consumables mix up 300 basis points to 68% of revenue, providing margin tailwinds.

Turning to geography, highlighting our balanced global footprint: U.S. 52%, EMEA 22%, APAC 18%, and Emerging Markets 8%.

U.S. organic growth accelerated to 11.3%, our best in two years, driven by elective procedure normalization—outpatient surgeries now at 115% of 2019 levels per Definitive Healthcare data. CVI and AST led here, with TAVR volumes plus 18% amid lower denial rates post our CMS advocacy on inappropriate use criteria. Pricing was resilient at plus 2%, though site-neutral payment policies pose risks into 2025.

EMEA grew 7.6% organically, with strength in Germany and the UK offsetting French reimbursement delays on orthopaedics. EU MDR compliance gave us a first-mover edge in next-gen stents, boosting CVI plus 14%. We're leveraging the UK's NHS productivity push for Hugo RAS pilots, targeting 20 hospital conversions by year-end.

APAC delivered 6.8% growth, tempered by China's zero-COVID hangover and National Reimbursement Drug List pricing pressures. Ex-China APAC shone at plus 12%, led by Japan's aging demographics fueling TAVR plus 20% and India's orthopaedics boom via our low-cost Triad implants. China CVI grew just 2%, but we're optimistic on pipeline approvals—like RhythmSync—for H1 2025 reimbursement inclusion, mirroring Dexcom's CGM success there.

Emerging Markets expanded 14.2%, our fastest-growing region, powered by LATAM vascular access ports and Brazil's spine fusions. Strategic partnerships, like our JV with a local distributor in Mexico for Hugo training centers, are scaling adoption amid rising middle-class healthcare spend.

This quarter underscores our Innovate, Penetrate, Expand framework. We're investing 8.5% of revenue in R&D, with 40% focused on AI/ML integration—e.g., predictive analytics in our EvoFlow valve for real-time deployment feedback, reducing paravalvular leak rates by 30% in bench tests. We're addressing supply chain resilience post-Taiwan tensions by dual-sourcing nitinol components, which mitigated 1 point of potential drag. Market-wise, we're gaining 120 basis points of share in U.S. CVI per NPM data, but face headwinds from GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic crimping bariatrics-adjacent ortho volumes short-term. Long-term tailwinds include a $650B addressable market growing 5-6% CAGR through 2030, per Evaluate MedTech, with minimally invasive shifts favoring our portfolio. For Q4, we guide organic growth to 8-10%, with full-year at 8.5%. We'll lap tough comps but expect continued volume momentum and 50 bps mix expansion.

Now, let's talk about SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

We delivered another quarter of strong top-line growth, with global revenues up 12% year-over-year to $1.8 billion, driven by our structural heart portfolio—particularly the CardioFlow TAVR valve, which gained 25% market share in the U.S. intermediate-risk segment—and robust uptake of our neuromodulation platforms like the NeuroStim DBS system amid rising referrals for essential tremor cases. But what really sets this quarter apart is our disciplined execution on the bottom line, particularly in SG&A, where we achieved meaningful efficiency gains while protecting our go-to-market capabilities.

SG&A expenses came in at $468 million for the quarter, up just 5% year-over-year on a reported basis, but flat sequentially despite 3% foreign exchange headwinds from a stronger USD against the euro and yen. As a percentage of revenue, SG&A deleveraged 190 basis points to 26%, marking the lowest level in five years and well ahead of our peers like Boston Scientific and Edwards Lifesciences, who are still hovering around 28-30%. This represents approximately $45 million in incremental savings versus our prior-year run rate, fully offsetting investments in our U.S. field safety team expansions ahead of the CMS bundled payment pilots for TAVR procedures.

Breaking it down, selling expenses, which comprise 65% of SG&A, grew only 4% to $304 million, reflecting a 15% improvement in sales force productivity. Our rep-to-procedure ratio improved to 1:28 from 1:24 a year ago, thanks to targeted territory realignments and the rollout of our AI-powered CRM platform, CoreSell AI, built on Salesforce Einstein and integrated with our procedure enablement tools. This has enabled 20% faster case coverage planning, reducing windshield time by 12%—critical in orthopedics and spine, where Stryker and Zimmer Biomet continue to face rep burnout amid surgeon consolidation. Digital demos for our minimally invasive robotics adjuncts, like the FlexiArm endoscopic system, now account for 35% of pre-op engagements, cutting travel costs by $18 million annualized.

On the G&A side, expenses were down 2% to $112 million, driven by procurement synergies from our global sourcing initiative. We captured $22 million in savings through a zero-based budgeting refresh, renegotiating contracts with key suppliers like DuPont for balloon catheter polymers and 3M for sterilization consumables—margins expanded 80 bps as a result. Our shared services center in Manila, now handling 70% of AP/AR processing via RPA bots from UiPath, delivered a 25% reduction in back-office FTEs without impacting service levels. IT efficiencies were another bright spot: migrating our ERP to SAP S/4HANA yielded $15 million in annual run-rate savings by streamlining inventory visibility for just-in-time stocking of high-volume stents and leads, mitigating the supply chain disruptions we've all seen post-Hurricane Helene impacts on Puerto Rico manufacturing.

Regionally, this plays out differently but consistently. In the U.S., which is 55% of revenues, SG&A as a percent of sales fell to 24.5%, bolstered by value-based care tailwinds. Our dedicated VBC teams—now 150 strong—focus on ACO partnerships for our WatchGuard remote monitoring platform, reducing field visits by 18% while boosting adherence rates to 92%, ahead of Medtronic's disclosed 88%. Europe, at 25% of mix, saw SG&A flat at €120 million despite MDR compliance ramp costs for our next-gen ICDs; efficiencies from harmonized commercial ops across our Dublin hub offset a 5% pricing haircut under the new German diagnosis-related group reforms. In emerging markets—China and LATAM, growing 22% to $180 million—we leveraged telemedicine pilots for our portable ultrasound line, trimming distributor commissions by 8 points and SG&A to 22% of regional sales, positioning us ahead of Mindray's aggressive localization push.

Strategically, these gains aren't one-offs; they're baked into our Efficient Growth 2026 framework. We're targeting another 100-150 bps of SG&A deleverage next year through three levers: scaling AI-driven analytics for high-value account targeting, prioritizing top-quartile IDNs like Kaiser and Cleveland Clinic; expanding our gig economy model for clinical specialists, akin to Intuitive Surgical's Flex Model for da Vinci training, to flex costs with procedure volumes; and cross-portfolio synergies, like bundling our cardio and neuro franchises under unified key account managers to capture 10-15% more wallet share. In short, we've transformed SG&A from a drag to a tailwind, funding 60% of our $250 million share repurchase this quarter while maintaining GAAP EPS growth of 18%. This positions us exceptionally well against macro headwinds like potential U.S. election-driven reimbursement tweaks or EU IVDR delays.

Moving on to procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

As we dive into our results, procedure volume trends and our perspective on market recovery continue to be the bedrock of our growth story in the Medical Devices sector. Overall, we saw robust procedure volume growth across our key franchises, reflecting a sustained post-pandemic rebound that's now firmly in expansionary territory. Globally, elective and semi-elective procedure volumes grew 14% year-over-year in Q3, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit gains and surpassing our pre-COVID baseline by approximately 8%. This performance underscores the durability of demand in high-acuity areas like structural heart, orthopedics, and neuromodulation, even amidst macroeconomic headwinds such as persistent inflation and hospital labor constraints.

By segment, starting with our largest contributor, Cardiovascular Interventions at 42% of Q3 revenue. Procedure volumes here expanded 16% YoY, driven by strong adoption of our next-gen TAVR platforms, including the CoreValve Evolut Pro+ and our recently launched low-profile FX delivery system. In the U.S., TAVR volumes were up 22% YoY, fueled by expanded CMS reimbursement for lower-risk patients under the TAVR 2.0 pathway and a shift toward ambulatory surgery centers, where we're capturing over 25% market share. This aligns with industry trends seen at peers like Edwards Lifesciences and Medtronic. Internationally, structural heart procedures grew 12%, with notable strength in Japan following the PMDA approval of our Evolut FX variant, offsetting softer EMEA volumes impacted by NHS backlog prioritization in the UK.

In Orthopedics and Spine, driving 28% of revenue, volumes rose 13% YoY globally. Hip and knee replacements—our Mako robotic-arm enabled procedures—surged 19% in the U.S., benefiting from pent-up demand resolution and our triad of enabling technologies: the Mako Total Knee 2.0 software update, which improved OR throughput by 15% via AI-optimized implant planning, and our Triathlon Total Knee System with OXINIUM oxidized zirconium for enhanced longevity. We're now at 1.2 systems per 100k population penetration in the U.S., up from 0.9 last year, positioning us competitively against Stryker's Mako fleet and Zimmer Biomet's ROSA platform. Spine procedures, particularly minimally invasive fusions with our VertiFlex Superion interspinous spacers, grew 11%, though we saw some moderation in elective laminectomies due to surgeon staffing shortages—a sector-wide issue echoed in recent Intuitive Surgical earnings.

In Electrophysiology and Neuromodulation, volumes were up 15% YoY, highlighting the resilience of chronic therapy segments. Our Watchman FLX left atrial appendage closure device saw U.S. implants jump 28%, capturing share from Boston Scientific's Watchman amid OUS expansion into CE Mark countries. Neuromodulation, powered by our Inceptiv closed-loop spinal cord stimulator, grew 18% in the U.S. pain management market, where we're leveraging real-world evidence from the SENZA-PDN pivotal trial to drive adoption in diabetic neuropathy—a $5B addressable market growing at 12% CAGR per IQVIA data.

Regionally, the recovery narrative remains bifurcated but overwhelmingly positive. In the U.S., representing 58% of our procedure volume, we posted 18% YoY growth, well ahead of the 12-14% industry average tracked by Definity Health. This was propelled by normalized hospital capacity—OR utilization now at 92% versus 78% in Q2 2022—and a 20% uptick in outpatient procedures under the No Surprises Act. Medicare Advantage penetration, now at 52% of eligible lives, has accelerated value-based care shifts, boosting ASPs by 3% for our bundle offerings.

Europe, at 22% of volumes, grew a solid 9% YoY, though tempered by energy costs and reimbursement headwinds. Germany and France led with 12% gains in orthopedics, supported by our DiGNR8 digital surgery platform integration with Siemens Healthineers' navigation systems. The UK lagged at 5%, as NHS waiting lists—still 7.6 million per latest DOH figures—prioritize cancer over electives, but our strategic partnership with Spire Healthcare for ASCs is yielding early wins, with 15% volume growth in private-pay segments.

Asia-Pacific ex-China volumes rose 11%, with Australia and India shining on the strength of our endoscopy portfolio, including the GI Genius AI polyp detection module, which improved adenoma detection rates by 22% in ASGE trials and drove 25% procedure uptake. China, post-zero-COVID, exploded 27% YoY—our strongest market—led by 35% growth in structural heart via our JV with Lepu Medical. National Reimbursement Drug List inclusion for our CorePulse ICDs has unlocked 500K annual addresses, positioning us for 20%+ organic growth through 2025.

Emerging markets like LATAM and MENA contributed 8% volume growth, bolstered by our affordable orthopedics line, the Trinity Advanced Bearing System, tailored for high-volume public hospitals.

Strategically, we're leaning into three tailwinds to sustain this momentum. First, digital enablement: Our OR 360 ecosystem, integrating IoT sensors with generative AI for predictive scheduling, reduced case cancellations by 18% in beta sites and is rolling out to 200 U.S. hospitals by year-end. This mirrors Intuitive's da Vinci 5 AI enhancements and positions us for the $15B digital surgery market by 2030, per Grand View Research.

Second, we're accelerating robotics and minimally invasive shifts. Mako case volume hit 1.1 million globally cumulative, with Q3 utilization up 14% to 22 cases per system per month. Investments in structural heart robotics—$250M committed over two years—target the 30% of TAVR procedures still hybrid-open.

Third, resilience plays: Amid hospital margin pressures (average U.S. hospital EBITDA at 4.2% per Kaufman Hall), our outcome-based pricing models, like the 2-year warranty on neuromodulation devices, have secured 40% of new contracts, mitigating ASP erosion risks.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 procedure volumes to grow 12-14% YoY globally, with U.S. at 16-18%, moderating slightly on seasonal flu impacts but supported by 50 new product launches, including our AI-driven PulseSense wearable for remote rhythm monitoring. Risks remain—reimbursement cliffs like the 2025 MPFS proposed 2.8% cut and cybersecurity vulnerabilities post-Change Healthcare—but our 22% market share in high-growth segments and $1.2B cash position for M&A de-risk us. In summary, procedure volumes are not just recovering; they're reaccelerating, validating our innovation-led strategy in a $600B+ industry poised for 6-7% CAGR through the decade.

Next, competitive dynamics and market share trends.

Our competitive dynamics and market share trends continue to underscore the resilience and leadership position of MediCore Devices in the $520 billion global medical devices market, growing at a robust 6.2% CAGR through 2028, per latest Grand View Research data. Despite macroeconomic headwinds like inflation and supply chain disruptions, we've methodically expanded our footprint across high-growth segments—cardiovascular, orthopedics, and robotics—gaining 120 basis points of share year-over-year to 8.2% globally, driven by our innovation pipeline and disciplined execution.

The industry is undergoing a structural shift toward minimally invasive procedures, value-based care models, and digital integration, fueled by aging demographics and rising chronic disease prevalence. In cardiovascular, which represents 45% of our revenue and 35% of the total market, procedure volumes grew 9% globally in Q3, per Procedure Pulse data. We're capitalizing here with our flagship TAVR platform, the PrecisionFlow Valve, which captured 28% U.S. market share in structural heart—up from 24% a year ago—edging out Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien series at 32% and Medtronic's Evolut at 25%. This gain reflects our 15% reduction in procedure times via next-gen docking technology and a 92% one-year durability rate in our STRIVE registry, outperforming the industry benchmark of 88%.

Orthopedics tells a similar story of share accretion. Amidst softening elective volumes due to reimbursement pressures under CMS's Site-Neutral Payment policies, our robotic-assisted systems, including the OrthoNav 4.0 platform, grew 18% YoY to 22% share in U.S. knee arthroplasty robotics, surpassing Stryker's Mako at 19% and Zimmer Biomet's ROSA at 15%. Key to this was our Q2 launch of AI-driven implant planning software, which improved surgical precision by 22% in precision scoring metrics and reduced revision rates to under 1.5% at two years—data from our 5,000-patient PROSPECT trial. Globally, orthopedics market share held steady at 12%, but we're targeting 15% by 2026 through expanded indications into spine and trauma.

Competitive dynamics are intensifying, particularly from big tech-medical crossovers and China incumbents. Intuitive Surgical maintains a commanding 85% share in soft-tissue surgical robotics with da Vinci, but our hybrid cardio-robotics system, CardioBot-X, is eroding that in hybrid ORs, securing 14% share in EP ablations and growing 25% QoQ. Boston Scientific's FARAPULSE pulsed-field ablation has pressured legacy RF players like Biosense Webster (J&J), but our Symplicity Spyral renal denervation device hit 30% EU share post-CE Mark, with U.S. IDE enrollment at 80% complete—positioning us for FDA approval in H1 2025. Chinese players like MicroPort and Peijia are aggressive in APAC, undercutting on price by 30-40%, but our premium positioning and local manufacturing in Suzhou have stabilized our 11% regional share.

Regionally, the U.S. remains our fortress, contributing 52% of revenue with 10.5% overall share, up 150 bps YoY. CMS's 2024 IPPS final rule boosted pass-through payments for our next-gen stents by 4.2%, enabling 12% procedure growth despite competitor pricing wars. In EMEA, at 28% of revenue, we're at 7.8% share, gaining traction post-Brexit with UK NHSE tenders—our neurostimulation leads, NeuroPulse, won 35% of the £250M neuromodulation framework, outpacing Medtronic's Intellis. Challenges persist from MDR delays, which slowed approvals by 18 months for rivals like Abbott's Navitor TAVR, giving us a first-mover edge.

APAC, our fastest-growing region at 20% of revenue and 22% YoY growth, sees us at 6.4% share amid a 12% market expansion. China's NMPA fast-track for high-volume devices propelled our TAVR volumes 35% higher, countering Lepu Medical's 20% share in domestic valves. In Japan, under the PMDA's Sakigake designation, our robotic platform secured JPY 15B in hospital contracts, lifting share to 18% from 12%. India and SEA remain nascent but promising, with our affordable ortho implants gaining 10% share via J&J partnerships.

Strategically, we're not standing still. Our $1.2B R&D spend—12% of revenue—funds 15 Phase III trials and 20+ IDEs, including bioresorbable scaffolds challenging Absorb's legacy issues with 95% patency at 3 years. M&A remains opportunistic: our $450M acquisition of NeuroDyn bolstered neuromodulation to 16% share, adding $120M in synergies. We're also advancing digital twins via AWS integration for predictive analytics, reducing time-to-market by 25%. Reimbursement savvy is key—lobbying for NTAP status on three devices secured an extra $50M in FY24 revenue. Looking forward, we see 200-300 bps of additional share gains over the next 24 months, targeting 10% globally by 2026. Risks include tariff escalations on titanium imports (mitigated by 70% domestic sourcing) and antitrust scrutiny on robotics consolidation. But with a pipeline of 12 blockbusters, gross margins expanding 210 bps to 68%, and ROIC at 15%, we're well-positioned to outpace peers.

Then, strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

Before we move further, I'd like to provide a detailed overview of our strategic priorities and focus areas for the upcoming quarter, Q4 FY2024. As you know, MediCore Devices is a leader in cardiovascular and orthopedic medical devices, with a portfolio spanning next-generation drug-eluting stents like our flagship InnoStent Neo, robotic-assisted surgical systems such as the RoboOrtho platform, and AI-enhanced diagnostic imaging tools. We've delivered 12% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3, driven by a 15% surge in U.S. structural heart procedures and 9% in EMEA orthopedics, but we're not resting on our laurels. Our Q4 priorities are laser-focused on accelerating innovation, optimizing our global footprint, enhancing operational resilience, and capturing share in high-growth segments amid a market projected to expand at 6.8% CAGR through 2028, per Grand View Research.

First and foremost, advancing our innovation pipeline and R&D acceleration, with 45% of Q4 CapEx allocation. We're doubling down on R&D to fuel our 15-18% organic growth target for FY2025. In Q4, we'll allocate $185 million—or 14.2% of projected quarterly revenue—to pipeline milestones, up from 12.8% in Q3. Key initiatives include cardiovascular franchise expansion: on track for FDA IDE approval and first-in-human trials for InnoStent Ultra, our bioresorbable scaffold with 30% faster endothelialization rates versus competitors like Abbott's Absorb BVS successor. Early benchtop data shows 25% reduction in late thrombosis risk, addressing the 2-3% annual restenosis rates plaguing current DES platforms. We'll invest $45 million in Q4 to scale manufacturing at our Galway, Ireland facility, targeting 20% U.S. market share in complex PCI by YE2025.

Robotics and AI integration: Building on RoboOrtho system's 28% procedural efficiency gains—mirroring Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci metrics—we're rolling out AI-driven predictive analytics for implant placement. Q4 will see the launch of RoboOrtho AI 2.0 in 150 U.S. sites, with partnerships alongside Stryker's Mako platform for hybrid ortho-cardio workflows. Expect $60 million in R&D here, aiming for 35% attach rate on our $2.5 billion ortho TAM.

Diagnostics innovation: Our AI-powered CardioScan imaging suite, which improved diagnostic accuracy by 22% in NAFLD detection trials, will enter EU MDR Phase III validation. We're targeting CE Mark by quarter-end, with $30 million earmarked for algorithm refinements using federated learning to comply with GDPR data sovereignty. These efforts align with industry trends: the shift to value-based care under CMS's MDCR program, where devices demonstrating 10-15% cost savings in readmissions—like our platforms—command premium reimbursements.

Second, regional market penetration and geographic diversification, targeting 22% international revenue mix. Geopolitically, we're navigating U.S. election-year uncertainties and EU MDR headwinds, but Q4 growth levers are clear. U.S. remains 62% of revenue at $1.2 billion projected, with focus on expanding in the $18 billion structural heart market. We'll deploy 25% more sales reps in the Southeast, targeting 12% growth amid 7% procedure volume uptick from aging demographics (65+ cohort growing 3.2% YoY per Census data).

EMEA (25% of revenue): Post-Brexit, prioritizing Germany and France, where ortho procedures rose 11% in H1 per EFORT stats. Q4 goal: 14% growth via 50 new hospital contracts for RoboOrtho, offsetting 5% reimbursement cuts in Italy. Our Galway hub will support just-in-time inventory, reducing lead times by 18%.

APAC (10% of revenue, high-growth focus): China and Japan represent our $300 million runway. Despite CFDA delays, we'll launch InnoStent Neo in 40 additional Tier-1 hospitals, leveraging our JV with Mindray for localized manufacturing. India pilots show 40% adoption in mid-tier cities; Q4 investment of $25 million targets 25% YoY growth, capitalizing on 9% CAGR in emerging markets per IQVIA.

Latin America and MEA emerging plays: $15 million for distributor expansions in Brazil and UAE, chasing 20% growth in value-segment stents amid 15% procedure inflation.

Third, operational excellence and supply chain fortification, EBITDA margin expansion to 28%. Margins hit 26.2% in Q3, but Q4 targets 28% through $120 million in gross savings. Supply chain disruptions—echoing 2022's resin shortages that hit peers like Boston Scientific—are top-of-mind. Initiatives: Reshoring and diversification: 60% of critical titanium alloys now sourced from U.S./EU vendors, up from 40%. Q4: Finalize $50 million automation at our Minnesota plant, cutting ortho implant COGS by 12% via Six Sigma robotics.

Digital transformation: ERP rollout with SAP S/4HANA to yield 8% inventory reduction. Pricing discipline—selective 3-5% hikes on high-margin products—offsets 4% raw material inflation.

Sustainability and ESG: Aligning with SEC climate disclosures, we'll certify 80% of devices as carbon-neutral, targeting Stryker-level ESG premiums in procurement.

Fourth, strategic partnerships, M&A, and capital deployment ($500M dry powder). M&A remains opportunistic: eyeing bolt-ons in neuromodulation (e.g., akin to Medtronic's InterStim expansions) with $300 million allocated. Q4 pipeline includes two LOIs for digital health startups enhancing our AI stack. Partnerships: Deepening co-development with Philips for hybrid OR imaging, projecting $100 million in cross-sell by FY2026.

Heads-up on headwinds: Potential U.S. tariff escalations could add 2% to APAC COGS; we'll hedge 70% forex exposure. Regulatory: 95% compliance on 510(k)s, but MDR audits loom. Upside: Tailwinds from 5.2% U.S. procedure growth per Definitive Healthcare. In summary, Q4 is about execution: innovate relentlessly, penetrate smartly, operate leanly, and deploy capital surgically. This positions us for 13-15% revenue growth and 30% ROIC, outpacing med device peers.

Finally, key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Before turning to Maria, let me walk you through the key assumptions underpinning our full-year guidance, which we are maintaining today: fiscal 2024 revenue of $32.8 billion to $33.2 billion, representing 5% to 6% organic growth at constant exchange rates; adjusted operating margin expansion of 50 basis points to 24.5%; and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $5.35 to $5.45. These targets reflect our disciplined execution amid a dynamic macroeconomic backdrop, but they're predicated on several core assumptions across market dynamics, procedural volumes, pricing, supply chain stability, and strategic initiatives.

On organic revenue growth drivers, we're assuming mid-single-digit global procedure growth of 4% to 5% across our key franchises—Cardiovascular, Neuroscience, Medical Surgical, and Diabetes—aligning with IQVIA and Procedure Volume Index data showing sustained post-pandemic recovery. Specifically, in Structural Heart, we're baking in 10% to 12% organic growth, driven by TAVR procedure volumes expanding 8% globally, mirroring trends seen with competitors like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform and our own CoreValve Evolut FX launches. This assumes U.S. TAVR penetration reaches 85% of eligible severe aortic stenosis patients, per ACC guidelines, with Europe adding tailwinds from expanded CE Mark indications for low-risk patients.

Diabetes growth of 7% to 9% hinges on continuous glucose monitoring sensor attach rates improving to 65% among type 2 diabetics on insulin, fueled by our MiniMed 780G system's algorithm upgrades enabling 1.5x more time-in-range versus prior gens. We're assuming U.S. reimbursement parity under Medicare Part B, similar to Dexcom's G7 traction.

Neurosense (Spinal and Neuromodulation) at 6% to 8%, supported by INTRACEPT procedure adoption for vertebrogenic pain—now with Level 1 evidence from our pivotal trial—and our Mimix hydroxyapatite-coated interbody devices capturing 15% U.S. share in lumbar fusion, akin to Globus Medical's ExcelsiusGPS robotics momentum.

MedSurg growth of 4% to 6%, with endoscopy volumes rebounding 5% on GI procedure backlogs and our Hugo RAS system's early U.S. soft-tissue pilots converting to 20% of bariatric cases by year-end.

We're also assuming new product revenue contributes 4% to 5% of total sales, up from 3.5% last year, driven by FDA approvals for our next-gen Percept PC neurostimulator with BrainSense tech and the Symplicity Spyral renal denervation catheter for hypertension.

Pricing and mix assumptions are critical. We expect core pricing to be flat to down 1% in the U.S. due to ongoing Medicare site-neutral payment reforms under the CY2024 OPPS final rule, which compresses hospital outpatient ASPs by 2.3% for devices like our pacemakers. However, this is offset by a 150 basis point favorable mix shift toward higher-ASP structural interventions (e.g., TAVR kits at $35,000 average) and premium robotics. In constant currency terms, we're modeling a 1% FX headwind, assuming EUR/USD at 1.08, GBP/USD at 1.25, and CNY/USD at 7.20—less severe than the 2% drag we faced in Q2.

Regional commentary underscores our diversified footprint: U.S. (58% of revenue): 5% to 7% organic growth on procedure recovery, but tempered by 1.5% ASP erosion from commercial payor pushback on bundled payments for orthopedics, à la UnitedHealth's Optum model.

EMEA (25%): 6% to 8% growth, with Germany and France driving endoscopy via DRG optimizations and our Affera mapping system's Prudent adoption for AFib ablations.

APAC (17%): Double-digit 12% to 14% expansion, led by China NMPA approvals for three new pipeline products (e.g., our EverFlex vascular stent), aging demographics boosting diabetes prevalence to 150 million cases by 2030 per IDF Atlas, and India's laparoscopic surge post-COVID.
